title: Post-cutover API key lease mismatch causes intermittent authz shadowing across nodes
creator: Anika Patel
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent 403s and cross-organization request acceptance after a scheduled rolling cutover. The issue manifests when an ingress/node that has been restarted accepts requests bound to API keys that were rotated or partially revoked on the control plane because its local lease cache contained an out-of-date lease epoch. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and rollback-safe fixes to ensure API key lease state cannot be replayed or accepted post-cutover.
incident_summary: 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC - Scheduled rolling cutover for dedicated-pool-12. Within the first hour, Customer A and Customer C reported intermittent authorization anomalies: requests from subaccounts returning 200 when they should have been rejected, and in other cases legitimate requests returning 403. Escalation to Platform SRE and Auth team. Root cause analysis indicates a lease-epoch mismatch between control plane lease table updates and node-local apikey lease caches during graceful restart. Affected nodes briefly accepted requests using stale org-scoping metadata until their caches reconciled (~30s-5m).
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate rolling restart of platform-ingress nodes while performing an API key rotation for a test tenant
Apply rotation to control plane and delay change propagation to node-local cache (introduce artificial network lag)
Send requests using the old key immediately after rotation; observe acceptance on restarted nodes with stale lease epoch
Verify that requests are accepted until node cache reconciliation completes or manual invalidation occurs
root_cause: Lease epoch mismatch and non-atomic local cache invalidation during node restart. The control plane updated apikey ownership and rotation epoch, but restarted nodes rehydrated caches from an eventually consistent store and temporarily considered an old lease valid. The token refresh / apikey acceptance path prioritized local cache truth without a fail-safe short-circuit to re-validate fresh rotations or revocations from the control plane during cutovers.
mitigation: Hotfix deployed (platform-ingress v1.14.3) that forces local cache revalidation on startup and on the first request post-cutover
Temporary circuit: any apikey rotation event triggers invalidation webhook to nodes in the cutover pool
Customer-facing mitigation: coordinated rolling cutover window extended and customers notified; PagerDuty escalation for affected accounts with manual cache flush instruction
fix_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12045 (ingress: force cache revalidation on post-startup requests)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12090 (add canary flag for incremental cache-invalidation rollout)
comments: 2026-03-04 - Anika Patel: Initial triage complete. Reproduced locally by simulating delayed propagation. Scoped to: apikey lease state + node-local cache rehydration logic. Assigning to Diego for hotfix + rollout plan.

2026-03-05 - Diego Morales: Implemented a conservative hotfix to invalidate cache on first request if node restart time within last 10m and control-plane epoch > local epoch. Running QA against dedicated test pool. Observed immediate reduction in acceptance of rotated keys.

2026-03-06 - SRE (Jamal Reed): Load test with 5000 concurrent tokens shows ~0.3% increased tail latency on first-request revalidation. Agreed acceptable for a rolling-window mitigation. Noted we need better reconciliation to avoid latency penalty in steady state.

2026-03-07 - PM (Laura Chen): Customer comms drafted; recommending prioritized canary for 5% of dedicated pools, then 25%, then full. Customers with active rotations to be contacted to reschedule if they cannot tolerate transient denials.
2026-03-08 - Security (Priya Nair): Confirmed hotfix reduces window for replay/acceptance. Full security review required for epoch-stamped writes; flagged for release gating.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Merged PRs to staging. Observability dashboards updated to surface 'last cache revalidation' and per-node lease epoch. Added automated smoke test into cutover job. Preparing rollout runbook.

2026-03-10 - Anika Patel: Customer A confirmed regression resolved after forced cache flush; closing their incident. Still seeing rare 1-in-10k occurrences in Dedicated-pool-9 during heavy rotation tests; next steps added below.
next_steps: Finish security review for epoch-stamped writes and get sign-off (security_review_required=true)
Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics gates (auth-acceptance-rate, 5xx rate, p99 latency)
Add stricter invariants: on rotation, control plane must push synchronous invalidation to nodes in the active cutover pool; if synchronous failure, abort rotation
Create automated integration test that simulates network partitions during rotation and ensures no acceptance of rotated/revoked keys
Post-release: run a migration job to bump lease epoch for nodes that persist stale leases and document for on-prem/private operators
acceptance_criteria: No customer-reported authz anomalies in two full cutover cycles across dedicated pools (observability: auth-acceptance-rate stable)
Automated regression tests covering rotation during node restart pass in CI (added to auth-service test matrix)
Security sign-off for epoch-stamped writes and invalidation webhook
Rollout runbook executed successfully in canary with defined metric gates
